gen-vast-shadow-gf-saira: Bent-paperclip lettering with a vintage grin, that's Vast Shadow, every stroke cut to a single width. Saira follows in a plain sans, its rounded forms stretching tall, and that gap between loud and level is the pair's best trick.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-sarpanch: Approachable is odd to say of a heading this showy, but Vast Shadow's strokes never swell or thin, which keeps it friendly. Sarpanch carries the longer reading in a contemporary sans, its open-mouthed e and compact lines moving along briskly.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Professional, yet Vast Shadow still looks vintage and loud. Its strokes have no thick and thin parts at all, while Schibsted Grotesk keeps big open e and a shapes for text, so one grabs attention and the other holds it.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-sen: Sen is a modern, tall-lowercase plain sans whose single constant line traces each letter and stops before curling inward. Vast Shadow's vintage display letters take the spotlight, though shrinking them would waste their spacing.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-sintony: Vintage and eye-catching, Vast Shadow cuts every letter at one width with generous space around it, while Sintony adds a chunky, tall midzone with smooth curves. The sharpest quality here is how differently they carry weight.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-sofia-sans: Cut-stencil swagger up top: Vast Shadow draws every stroke at one width with a tall mean line. And Sofia Sans, a plain sans with rounded, open-sided letters, follows without modulation; heading text at a big size lets both look their best.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-sofia-sans-semi-conde: Eye-catching from the first word, Vast Shadow has vintage display presence and generous spacing, while Sofia Sans Semi Condensed's lowercase nearly matches its capitals in height. One makes the loud statement; the other handles steady text.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-sono: Approachable, despite the vintage display heading: Vast Shadow has no thick-and-thin contrast to slow the eye, and so does Sono in its way. Sono's tall lowercase and widely spaced letters, with each a left ajar, keep a longer read loose and easy.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-spline-sans-mono: Vintage display letters meet code-style type: Vast Shadow's uniform strokes and tall mean line sit above Spline Sans Mono's fixed-width, bold lowercase. They share a single-width stroke, so the page feels cut from one stencil.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-stack-sans-notch: Rod-stock thickness runs through this pair, with Vast Shadow's vintage single-width strokes up top and a plain sans below. And Stack Sans Notch has open curves, while Vast Shadow earns its keep when it's big and short.
